case_name_unsealed_after_inference: Bundesverband der Verbraucherzentralen und Verbraucherverbande v Planet49 GmbH (C-673/17)

ratings.reason: Directive 2002/58/EC was identified and retrieved, but the answer-bearing amended Article 5(3) text and Article 2(f) chain were not recovered.
The system recovered and cited the active-consent rule, including that silence, pre-ticked boxes and inactivity do not constitute consent.

It reached the correct legal direction for the preselected checkbox and cited retrieved GDPR-derived structured evidence, but did not recover the direct amended ePrivacy provision connecting that rule to terminal-equipment access.

The final overview stated the correct rule, but the corresponding leaf abstained and supplied no supporting claim or evidence. The final assertion was therefore unsupported and internally inconsistent.
The system appropriately abstained, but did not recover or identify the cookie-duration information duty.
The system appropriately abstained, but did not recover or identify the third-party-access information duty.

It recovered the repeal/replacement date for Directive 95/46/EC and the continuing identity of Directive 2002/58/EC, but overgeneralized simultaneous applicability and did not establish the national temporal qualification.
It did not purport to decide the separate, unasked issue of whether lottery participation conditioned on advertising consent was freely given.
The final overview introduced the correct personal-data-independence proposition without a supporting claim, while its own detailed section said that point could not be established.

The preselected-checkbox conclusion aligned with the judgment, but the personal-data point was unsupported and the duration/third-party-access holdings were missed. The system did not overstate that it was deciding the national action.
